text:
jasper: Heads up — after rolling continuous-batcher v2 to 50% traffic we see prefix cache hit-rate drop ~18% for short prompt cohort (<=64 tokens). p95 latency up ~12ms. Anyone else seeing this?

maria: saw the alert. grabbing profiles now.

leo: what does the batch composition look like? v2 changed coalescing heuristics right?

jasper: yeah v2 groups by arrival-window then fills up to 64 tokens. It reduced tail for long sessions but seems to mix short+short-with-prefix-less often which might be hurting prefix reuse.

maria: quick dump from the trace:
```
batcher.v2.coalesce_ratio: 0.72
avg_batch_size: 11.3
short_prompt_fraction_in_batch: 0.48 -> 0.33 (pre-rollout 0.61)
prefix_cache.hits/req: 0.62 -> 0.51
p95_latency_ms: 86 -> 98
```

maria: profiler shows KV cache lookup rate unchanged but hit-per-key down. suggests key-churn rather than eviction.

leo: could be keying variance — v2 added session affinity tag to routing which changed 'prefix_key' composition?

jasper: v1 key was `model+prefix_sha1`, v2 we tacked `cohort_id` for affinity. commit 9f3a2d changed key format.

infra-bot: deploy-bot reported: continuous-batcher v2 canary start 2026-03-14T09:12Z (canary 5%), scaled to 50% at 2026-03-14T09:45Z.

leo: adding cohort_id can explode key space for short prefixes. if cohort_id has high cardinality, warmup won't hit.

maria: confirm — we see prefix_key cardinality up ~2.8x for the short cohort in the last hour. eviction not the main driver.

jasper: hmm. So tradeoff: affinity reduced latency for long flows but killed reuse for short prompts. Need to measure overall unit-cost impact.

tanya: can we try a hybrid keying rule: `model+prefix_sha1+(cohort_id if prefix_len>64)` so we only partition long prefixes?

leo: yep that's low-risk. should restore reuse for short prefixes. Also maybe warmup window: prefetch first-K tokens into KV cache on batch formation. v2 reduced prefetch to avoid extra mem pressure.

maria: ran a local microbench with hybrid keying + prefetch window 128: hit-rate back to 0.60 and p95 down 6ms. rough numbers: qps ~same, tokens/s slightly up.

jasper: nice. can you paste command?

maria: docker run perfbench --model redwood-mini --batcher coalesce=v2,affinity=0.6,prefetch=128 --workload short_cohort

leo: throw kernel selection notes in here: under mixed batches we sometimes pick the small-seq kernel which has higher per-token overhead vs fused long-kernel. when batch mixes short/long sequences kernels switch more often -> GPU kernel-init overhead. that also adds a few ms.

jasper: interesting — so continuous batching affects both cache locality and kernel churn. two axes to optimize.

tanya: proposed plan: 1) revert cohort_id in prefix key for prefixes <=64 2) restore prefetch=128 for short_cohort via policy 3) add a lightweight histogram to runtime to track key_cardinality_by_prefix_len 4) run canary for 12h and collect hit-rate/cost delta.

leo: also add a metric for 'kernel_switches_per_batch' (count of kernel types invoked per batch) — might correlate with p95.

jasper: +1. can someone open a quick PR with the keying change and an opt-in flag? want to test on canary before broader rollback.

maria: I'll open PR and attach perf run. PR will include the microbenchmark script and results.

deploy-bot: @maria opened PR #4127 (continuous-batcher: hybrid-keying + short-prefetch) — pipeline queued.

jasper: thanks. if the canary looks good we can keep v2 and tweak keying, not full rollback. prefer targeted fix. :thumbsup:

tanya: also capturing this as a follow-up for the perf retro. adding to eng-runtime board.

leo: one caution — if we keep cohort-affinity for long prefixes it still may fragment caches across hosts. consider adding cross-host warmup (replicate hot prefix keys) for top-K prefixes.

maria: noted. i'll include a short analysis of top-200 prefixes and host spread in PR notes.

jasper: great. will check results later today. :eyes:
